scope: Exact owned local database suspension and conditional resume recipes only; no observed cleanup or recovery outcome
reviewFindings: Suspension verifies exact ownership, PID file, cluster path, port and live database data-directory identity before pg_ctl.
Both databases must retain matching exact migration ledgers; build database must remain empty.
Full database must contain only the exact ten fixture actor identities, no sessions and no audit rows; other business state is captured with complete sorted digests.
Other client connections are rejected twice before stopping; unrelated processes are never targeted.
Only pg_ctl for the exact owned cluster performs stop/start. Database files and private synthetic fixtures remain retained; prior owner metadata is preserved before updating live ownership state.
Resume requires fresh passing capacity, absent PID file and free loopback port before startup.
Resume verifies build migration/emptiness and complete full-database business/session/audit digests against suspended state; no creation, migration, seeding or application call occurs.
Failure cleanup stops only the just-started owned PID when its exact cluster PID still matches.
sideEffects: New sanitized snapshot and result receipts under the package
Owned PostgreSQL stop or start and its local log/PID files
Preserved prior and updated current cluster-owner metadata
conditions: Do not infer success from admission; inspect actual suspend/resume and checkpoint receipts.
Do not resume while capacity fails.
If owner, PID, clients, paths or fixture state differ, stop and preserve evidence; do not broaden targets.
No production data, migration, secret output, deployment or unrelated process termination.
limitations: Database preparation and retained-state proof are not native authentication denial/positive evidence.
Stopping an idle cluster is not a successful database restore test.
The capacity gate remains a time-specific conservative heuristic.
